04Project 01

You handle the reps.
We handle the protein.

McDonald's launched a protein menu and talked macros. Nobody at the gym cares about macros, they care about the burger waiting after.

Role: Social Media Strategist (spec) Type: Integrated social campaign strategy Duration: 8 weeks

Campaign creative

The whole platform, at a glance.

The challenge

It was never about protein.

McDonald's built decades of equity on convenience and indulgence. A health menu doesn't undo that. The real question was never nutritional, it was cultural.

"How do you join fitness culture without pretending to be a fitness brand?"

The idea

Own the joke. Don't correct it.

Everyone already jokes about McDonald's after leg day. That's free distribution, not a brand problem. McGym just shows up where the joke already lives.

McGym™: not a new business. Just permission to join a joke that already existed.

Strategic objectives

Four things this had to do.

01

Get the protein menu in front of people who'd actually order it.

02

Make "balance" the association, not "diet."

03

Let the internet do the talking: earned over paid.

04

Turn a laugh into a restaurant visit.

Audience

Everyday fitness, not athletes.

Primary: Gen Z and young Millennials who lift, but won't let it define their order.

Secondary: Fitness creators and running crews who can vouch for it without sounding like an ad.

Campaign strategy

Three stages, one punchline.

01

Tease

McGym shows up before anyone's told what it is: signage, teaser films, zero explanation.

02

Reveal

The protein menu lands as the payoff, not the pitch. Hero films and creator demos do the talking.

03

Hand over

The brand steps back. The McGym Challenge lets the audience run with it.

Channel & creator strategy

Ten honest voices beat one paid one.

Organic carries the humor: memes, behind-the-scenes, creator bits. Paid does the unglamorous work: reach and retargeting.

No single ambassador, just micro creators across fitness, running and food. The goal was community validation, not influencer promotion.

Success framework

Beyond sales: sentiment that sticks.

Awareness

Reach · video completion · branded search

Engagement

UGC · creator performance · social conversation

Business impact

Menu sales · app engagement · repeat visits

•Reflection

"The strongest campaigns don't interrupt culture. They become part of it."

05Project 02

Great campaigns don't start with ads. They start with better thinking.

Marketing Academy taught the how, but gave no reason to see LinkedIn as more than a course library. So I repositioned it around a mindset: Think Before You Launch.

Role: Social Media Strategist (spec) Type: Integrated B2B go-to-market strategy Duration: 12 weeks

Campaign creative

The "Think Before You Launch" system.

The challenge

Nobody's short on information anymore.

New tool, new framework, every day. The problem isn't access to knowledge, it's knowing what's worth your attention before you hit publish.

"How does Marketing Academy become a mindset, not just a syllabus?"

The idea

Sell the transformation, not the syllabus.

Nobody brags about finishing a course. They brag about the campaign that worked. LinkedIn already owns the network. The bigger prize is owning the instinct behind good marketing.

Think Before You Launch. The courses show up once you're already thinking.

Strategic objectives

Four things this had to do.

01

Reach marketers who don't think they need a course.

02

Sell the shift in thinking, not the feature list.

03

Make LinkedIn the name people credit for the win.

04

Build advertisers who actually get the platform.

Audience

Every stage, one ambition.

Primary: Demand gen, performance and growth marketers who plan the campaign, not just run the ads.

Secondary: Founders, CMOs, and anyone one promotion away from B2B marketing.

Campaign strategy

From question, to habit, to conversation.

01

Question

A strategic question lands before any pitch does, interrupting the scroll on purpose.

02

Equip

Frameworks and campaign breakdowns turn that question into a habit worth keeping.

03

Discuss

Marketers start comparing notes, right where Academy lives.

Channel, creator & AI

Practitioners over instructors.

Organic runs on frameworks and planning prompts built to spark actual discussion. Paid covers the funnel: bold questions for awareness, testimonials for conversion.

Creator partners are working B2B marketers, not celebrities. AI speeds up research and reporting, but strategic thinking stays a human advantage.

Success framework
